person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the immediate psychological response of the general public in mainland China during the first weeks of the COVID-19 outbreak
span.quote: The aim of this study was to survey the general public in China to better understand their levels of psychological impact, anxiety, depression, and stress during the initial stage of the COVID-19 outbreak.

span.label: what levels of psychological impact, anxiety, depression and stress the Chinese general public showed in the initial stage of the outbreak, and what was associated with them
span.quote: The aim of this study was to survey the general public in China to better understand their levels of psychological impact, anxiety, depression, and stress during the initial stage of the COVID-19 outbreak.

span.label: a three-day snapshot of 1,210 respondents across 194 cities taken two weeks into the outbreak, with the associations that distinguish higher from lower psychological impact
span.quote: This study included 1210 respondents from 194 cities in China.

span.label: existence
span.quote: In total, 53.8% of respondents rated the psychological impact of the outbreak as moderate or severe; 16.5% reported moderate to severe depressive symptoms; 28.8% reported moderate to severe anxiety symptoms; and 8.1% reported moderate to severe stress levels.

span.label: population-level psychological distress during an epidemic, before any intervention has been designed for it
span.quote: The aim of this study was to survey the general public in China to better understand their levels of psychological impact, anxiety, depression, and stress during the initial stage of the COVID-19 outbreak.

span.label: anonymous online cross-sectional survey, snowball sampling from university students, 31 January to 2 February 2020, with IES-R and DASS-21 and univariate linear regressions
span.term: anonymous online cross-sectional survey, snowball sampling from university students, 31 January to 2 February 2020, with IES-R and DASS-21 and univariate linear regressions
span.quote: We adopted a cross-sectional survey design to assess the public’s immediate psychological response during the epidemic of COVID-19 by using an anonymous online questionnaire.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE INSTRUMENT SETS THE CEILING ON THE CLAIM: IES-R measures a stress reaction to a named event and DASS-21 measures self-reported state, so what the study can report is how people scored themselves during three days, not what their mental health was
span.quote: Psychological impact was assessed by the Impact of Event Scale-Revised (IES-R), and mental health status was assessed by the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (DASS-21).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: SNOWBALL SAMPLING FROM STUDENTS PROPAGATES THROUGH ONE NETWORK: the survey was seeded with university students and passed onward, so the sample inherits the structure of that network - which is why the authors report oversampling of peers and reduced generalisability to less educated people
span.quote: A snowball sampling strategy, focused on recruiting the general public living in mainland China during the epidemic of COVID-19, was utilized. The online survey was first disseminated to university students and they were encouraged to pass it on to others.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: ANONYMITY FORECLOSED THE FOLLOW-UP: ethical requirements on anonymity and confidentiality prevented collecting contact details, so the prospective study the authors say would be ideal was not merely unfunded but structurally impossible after the fact
span.quote: Furthermore, it would be ideal to conduct a prospective study on the same group of participants after a period. Due to ethical requirements on anonymity and confidentiality, we were not allowed to collect contact details and personal information from the respondents.

span.label: snowball sampling was adopted for speed and is not a random selection; the authors state the study population did not reflect the actual pattern of the general population
span.quote: Given the limited resources available and time-sensitivity of the COVID-19 outbreak, we adopted the snowball sampling strategy. The snowballing sampling strategy was not based on a random selection of the sample, and the study population did not reflect the actual pattern of the general population.

span.label: a prospective follow-up would have been ideal and was foreclosed by the anonymity requirement, which barred collecting contact details
span.quote: Furthermore, it would be ideal to conduct a prospective study on the same group of participants after a period. Due to ethical requirements on anonymity and confidentiality, we were not allowed to collect contact details and personal information from the respondents.

span.label: without the follow-up the study cannot provide concrete support for a focused public health initiative - the authors name what their own design cannot deliver
span.quote: As a result, we could not conduct a prospective study that would provide a concrete finding to support the need for a focused public health initiative.

span.label: oversampling of one peer network (students) produced selection bias, making the conclusion less generalisable, particularly to less educated people
span.quote: There was an oversampling of a particular network of peers (e.g., students), leading to selection bias. As a result, the conclusion was less generalizable to the entire population, particularly less educated people.

span.label: self-reported psychological impact, anxiety, depression and stress may not align with assessment by mental health professionals
span.quote: Another limitation is that self-reported levels of psychological impact, anxiety, depression and stress may not always be aligned with assessment by mental health professionals.

span.label: responses about satisfaction with health information and about precautionary measures may be socially desirable - which bears directly on the paper's policy-relevant finding
span.quote: Similarly, respondents might have provided socially desirable responses in terms of the satisfaction with the health information received and precautionary measures.

span.label: very few respondents had a contact history or had sought medical consultation, so the findings cannot be generalised to confirmed or suspected COVID-19 cases
span.quote: Lastly, the number of respondents with contact history and who had sought medical consultations was very small. Our findings could not be generalized to confirmed or suspected cases of COVID-19.

span.label: expedited ethics approval from an institutional review board, conforming to the Declaration of Helsinki, with informed consent from every respondent
span.note: eliminates: data collected without consent or oversight being reported as a population survey · outcome: held
span.quote: Expedited ethics approval was obtained from the Institutional Review Board of the Huaibei Normal University (HBU-IRB-2020-001), which conformed to the principles embodied in the Declaration of Helsinki.

span.label: the questionnaire was built from previously published SARS and influenza instruments rather than written fresh, with COVID-19 items added
span.note: eliminates: instrument novelty as a source of the prevalence figures - the questionnaire was built from previously published SARS and influenza instruments rather than written fresh · outcome: held
span.quote: Previous surveys on the psychological impacts of SARS and influenza outbreaks were reviewed \ [18, 21, 24\]. Authors included additional questions related to the COVID-19 outbreak.

span.label: all tests two-tailed at p < 0.05
span.note: eliminates: one-tailed testing chosen after seeing the direction of an effect - all tests were two-tailed at a stated threshold · outcome: held
span.quote: All tests were two-tailed, with a significance level of p < 0.05.

span.label: data collection was bounded to three days immediately after the WHO declared a public health emergency, so the snapshot has a fixed and stated position in the outbreak rather than spanning changing conditions
span.note: eliminates: changing epidemic conditions as a confound within the sample - collection was bounded to three days immediately after the WHO emergency declaration, so every respondent answered at the same point in the outbreak · outcome: held
span.quote: Data collection took place over three days (31 January–2 February 2020) after the WHO declared the COVID-19 outbreak as a public health emergency of international concern.

span.label: cross-sectional survey
span.quote: We adopted a cross-sectional survey design to assess the public’s immediate psychological response during the epidemic of COVID-19 by using an anonymous online questionnaire.

span.label: snowball sampling
span.quote: A snowball sampling strategy, focused on recruiting the general public living in mainland China during the epidemic of COVID-19, was utilized. The online survey was first disseminated to university students and they were encouraged to pass it on to others.

span.label: selection bias
span.quote: There was an oversampling of a particular network of peers (e.g., students), leading to selection bias. As a result, the conclusion was less generalizable to the entire population, particularly less educated people.

span.label: Impact of Event Scale-Revised
span.quote: Psychological impact was assessed by the Impact of Event Scale-Revised (IES-R), and mental health status was assessed by the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (DASS-21).

span.label: Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale
span.quote: Psychological impact was assessed by the Impact of Event Scale-Revised (IES-R), and mental health status was assessed by the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (DASS-21).

span.label: psychological impact
span.quote: Specific up-to-date and accurate health information (e.g., treatment, local outbreak situation) and particular precautionary measures (e.g., hand hygiene, wearing a mask) were associated with a lower psychological impact of the outbreak and lower levels of stress, anxiety, and depression (p < 0.05).

span.label: linear regressions
span.quote: We used linear regressions to calculate the univariate associations between sociodemographic characteristics, physical symptom and health service utilization variables, contact history variables, knowledge and concern variables, precautionary measure variables, additional health information variables, and the IES-S score as well as the subscales of the DASS.

span.label: precautionary measures
span.quote: Specific up-to-date and accurate health information (e.g., treatment, local outbreak situation) and particular precautionary measures (e.g., hand hygiene, wearing a mask) were associated with a lower psychological impact of the outbreak and lower levels of stress, anxiety, and depression (p < 0.05).

span.label: socially desirable responses
span.quote: Similarly, respondents might have provided socially desirable responses in terms of the satisfaction with the health information received and precautionary measures.

span.label: prospective study
span.quote: Furthermore, it would be ideal to conduct a prospective study on the same group of participants after a period. Due to ethical requirements on anonymity and confidentiality, we were not allowed to collect contact details and personal information from the respondents.

span.label: female gender, student status, specific physical symptoms and poor self-rated health → greater psychological impact and higher stress, anxiety and depression
span.note: AN ASSOCIATION MEASURED ON ONE DAY BY UNIVARIATE LINEAR REGRESSION, and the vocabulary has no `associated-with`. Every legal type here would be wrong in a different way: `causes` asserts a direction the design cannot see, `part-of` and `is-a` are category relations, `contrasted-with` says the paper set them against each other and it did not. THE COMMONEST RELATION IN QUANTITATIVE SOCIAL SCIENCE HAS NO HOME IN THE SCHEMA.
span.quote: Female gender, student status, specific physical symptoms (e.g., myalgia, dizziness, coryza), and poor self-rated health status were significantly associated with a greater psychological impact of the outbreak and higher levels of stress, anxiety, and depression (p < 0.05).

span.label: specific up-to-date accurate health information and particular precautionary measures such as hand hygiene and mask wearing → lower psychological impact and lower stress, anxiety and depression
span.note: The same shape and the direction that matters for policy, and the same problem. It is also the one a reader is most likely to misread as causal, because it names an ACTION and an OUTCOME - which is exactly why it must not be tagged `causes` on a cross-sectional design.
span.quote: Specific up-to-date and accurate health information (e.g., treatment, local outbreak situation) and particular precautionary measures (e.g., hand hygiene, wearing a mask) were associated with a lower psychological impact of the outbreak and lower levels of stress, anxiety, and depression (p < 0.05).

span.label: psychological impact - IN THIS PAPER A SCORE ON THE IMPACT OF EVENT SCALE-REVISED, an instrument built for post-traumatic stress reactions to a specific event, and NOT a clinical assessment. The authors say so themselves: self-reported levels may not align with assessment by mental health professionals
span.quote: Another limitation is that self-reported levels of psychological impact, anxiety, depression and stress may not always be aligned with assessment by mental health professionals.

span.label: associated with - THE PAPER'S OWN CEILING AND IT KEEPS TO IT EVERYWHERE. The design is cross-sectional and the analysis is UNIVARIATE linear regression, so nothing here is adjusted for anything else and no temporal order is observed. `Female gender ... associated with a greater psychological impact` is a difference between groups measured on one day
span.quote: We used linear regressions to calculate the univariate associations between sociodemographic characteristics, physical symptom and health service utilization variables, contact history variables, knowledge and concern variables, precautionary measure variables, additional health information variables, and the IES-S score as well as the subscales of the DASS.

span.label: the general public - RECRUITED FROM UNIVERSITY STUDENTS OUTWARD, which the authors name as oversampling one network of peers. The sample is 1,210 people across 194 cities and it is explicitly not a picture of the general population
span.quote: There was an oversampling of a particular network of peers (e.g., students), leading to selection bias. As a result, the conclusion was less generalizable to the entire population, particularly less educated people.
